Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to
on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If
applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the
agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s office during normal business
hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make
inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the
Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours
prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however,
to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a
presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council must
fill out a green speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits
the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific
agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City
Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of
items shown on the agenda.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  January 26, 2010

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Perkins.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Bird, Rea, Goodhart, Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey,
  Mayor Perkins

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Hoefgen, City Attorney Pannone, Assistant City
  Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  City Treasurer Sherwood, Minutes Secretary Monson

MAYOR’S REPORT – Matters of Community Interest

Mayor Perkins welcomed Boy Scout Troop 134. She also reminded the public of the next Mayor’s
Community Forum to be held on Tuesday, February 2nd, at 6:30 p.m.

CONSENT AGENDA

approved that the following Consent Agenda items be approved:

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Niki Tennant, representing Assembly Member Bonnie Lowenthal, provided an update on activities of
the office, including legislation authored by the Assembly Member and signed by the Governor. She
also repeated grim warnings on the fiscal status of the State and dire consequences of the anticipated
$21 billion budget shortfall.

CITY COUNCIL  2
 RESOLUTION R10-01; A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A REVISED FEE SCHEDULE
FOR SERVICES RENDERED RELATING TO BUILDING AND SAFETY, PLANNING
AND PUBLIC WORKS PERMITS

Assistant City Manager Smith reported that the City is permitted to recover the cost of providing
development services to ensure that the party requesting the services pays for the cost of these
services and not the general taxpayer. The methodology for evaluating these costs includes direct
and indirect cost components over a three year period. This year’s evaluation indicated an 18.4%
increase in fees is warranted. This year Planning related fees were looked at more closely due to an
increasing shortfall in this area. The evaluation showed PVE’s fees ranged from 22% to 66% lower
than the other surveyed cities. Staff recommended a 20% increase in Planning fees and a 10%
increase in Building fees. She noted that the 20% increase ranges from $17 to $265 for the most
common applications. There is a newly proposed fee classification related to Revised
Neighborhood Compatibility Applications. Once a property has been through Neighborhood
Compatibility (NC), any future changes or additions to the property are also subject to a
Neighborhood Compatibility Review. Currently, these applications pay half fees regardless of
when the original approval was processed. Staff proposed that once the original construction
associated with the NC approval is finaled, that any revised application would be subject to full
fees.

Councilmember Rea asked why the costs had increased. Director Rigg responded that the increases
are typically 2%-3% per year and there has not been a fee increase since 2006.

Councilmember Rea asked if the City tracked the number of Neighborhood Compatibility
applications that are approved the first time around, second time around, etc. He said that every
time a NC application goes before the Planning Commission there is staff time involved to work the
application. Director Rigg said that each subsequent time an application goes before the
Commission it is essentially free of charge, but it would be difficult to determine exactly what the
additional costs are. Also, it may put applicants in a difficult position to accept a continuance if
there was going to be an additional fee charged.

No members of the public wished to speak on the matter.

After Council discussion, it was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey, seconded by
Councilmember Goodhart, and unanimously approved to adopt Resolution R10-01 to adopt a
revised fee schedule for development services, which reflects a 20% increase in planning
application fees and a 10% increase in building and public works permit fees.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report
JANUARY 26, 2010
CITY COUNCIL  3
 City Manager Hoefgen advised of two items on the upcoming February 9th agenda: Presentation by
Southern California Edison on the “State of Electric Utility” and presentation of the 2009
Comprehensive Annual Financial Report and updated Fiscal Health Report. He also said the City
has held up well during the recent rain storms and thanked Streets and Parks staff for a job well
done.

DEMANDS

It was moved by Councilmember Rea and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey that the
demands, as approved by a majority of the City Council, totaling $224,312.64 be allowed and it was
unanimously approved.

It was moved by Councilmember Rea and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey that the
demands, as approved by a majority of the City Council No. 516828 to 516900 totaling $521,747.38
be allowed and it was unanimously approved.

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS’ REPORTS

Mayor Perkins attended the Re-Opening and Dedication of the PVPUSD Malaga Cove Administration
Center earlier in the day along with Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey, Councilmember Goodhart,
Councilmember Bird and City Manager Hoefgen. She said it is a beautiful facility and great addition
to the City of PVE. She also spoke at the Breakfast Club on the State of the City where she was asked
about the traffic in Malaga Cove in the afternoons. She would like the Council to look into the
situation. She, along with Councilmember Goodhart and City Manager Hoefgen, attend the SBCCOG
workshop on regional agencies.

Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey will be attending the City Selection Committee Meeting on February 4th
and she asked for the Council’s concurrence to nominate and cast the City’s vote for Judy Mitchell as
representative to the Air Quality Management District.

Councilmember Bird mentioned that the Malaga Cove Homeowners’ Association is fundraising to help
the school district landscape the new MC Administration Center.

Councilmember Goodhart reported on his attendance at the League of California Cities policy
committee meetings for Public Safety and Environmental Quality held in Sacramento February 20-22.
Copies of his notes from the meeting will be distributed to the City Council.
